what: Alcoa mines bauxite, refines it into alumina, and smelts alumina into aluminium, selling the metal to carmakers, packaging firms, builders and electrical manufacturers.
customers: Aluminium buyers worldwide; the metal trades at a world price set on the London Metal Exchange.
moat: Bauxite mines and smelters with access to cheap, mostly hydroelectric, power, which is what decides who survives when the aluminium price falls.
risks: Aluminium and alumina prices set the results entirely and are volatile
Energy is the largest smelting cost, so power prices move the margin
$2.7B of debt against $1.6B of cash in a cyclical business
opportunities: 6.1 times earnings and 4.0 times EBITDA with $890M of free cash flow
Analysts see about 55% upside, with 13 covering the stock
Tariffs on imported aluminium have widened the American premium, which Alcoa's domestic smelters capture
watch: The aluminium price and the American Midwest premium, plus smelter energy costs.
